premises.text: Even heavy cloud-app users keep email central, and attachments trapped in email become a content silo that wastes space and slows work
premises.evidence_span: email is a massive content silo. Stuff just gets stuck in there

premises.text: Cloudless connects email to cloud services so attachments move into the right folders while staying linked to email context, including automated rules and secure cloud attach with access controls
premises.evidence_span: she could move these files directly into other cloud services and keep them associated with the context of the original email

premises.text: Admins can onboard teams, set cross-application data-handling policies, and gain visibility into ownership and workflows via an event dashboard
premises.evidence_span: she sets policies across the cloud applications that they use so that she can make sure that data is being consistently handled

premises.text: Cloudless expands toward a platform that pulls data on demand between cloud services (e.g., autofill Salesforce from email)
premises.evidence_span: Think of Cloudless as the beginnings of a platform where you can pull data on demand from any cloud service into any other cloud service

premises.text: Product is free for individuals; customers pay when they claim a group and govern data workflow across them
premises.evidence_span: Cloudless is completely free for individual users. You only pay when you claim a group of people and you govern the data workflow across them

value.text: Users and IT get simple, secure workflow across the enterprise cloud with interconnectivity and visibility
value.evidence_span: Cloudless offers a simple, secure workflow across the enterprise cloud that users and IT will love

notes: Manual move, multi-file, auto-rules, and ACL attach folded as one email-cloud workflow mechanism (§4.1.7). Cross-service platform examples coded as an asserted future path, not mere vision fluff, because speaker frames them as what Cloudless enables.
